title: introduce-pluggable-attn-adapter-and-rope-rotary-stitching
author: Daniel Hsu
release_notes: Adds a pluggable attention adapter, runtime kernel probing, and a fused rope->rotary stitching path that yields latency improvements for mixed-length workloads. Backwards-compatible fallbacks retained.
description:
Motivation: runtime needs to pick the best attention kernel variant for heterogeneous workloads without a heavy rollout. This PR introduces a pluggable attention adapter interface plus a small fused operator (rope->rotary stitch) and a kernel-probing harness so the scheduler can prefer the fused path when beneficial. The goal is lower p99 latency for mixed token lengths and more predictable tail-latency by moving compatibility checks out of the hot path.

What this does (high-level): - Introduce AttnAdapter interface to abstract kernel selection and probing. - Implement a CUDA probe kernel and lightweight C++ probe harness that records supported fused ops and numeric profiles. - Add a rope->rotary stitching fused op (rope_stitch) implemented with vectorized kernels for small rotary sizes. - Update the request router/scheduler to consult AttnAdapter decisions and prefer fused paths when they meet latency/cost heuristics. - Add deterministic unit and microbench tests, perf harness results, and docs for opt-in rollout.

Checklist: - [x] AttnAdapter API and unit tests - [x] probe kernel + safety timeouts - [x] rope_stitch operator (+ fallback) - [x] scheduler integration + policy toggle - [x] docs and perf notes - [x] benchmarks on Ampere and Hopper instances - [x] CI green after one rerun

Commits (summary): - Add AttnAdapter interface and base impl (adapter.py + adapter.h) - Kernel probe probe_kern.cu and C++ harness (probe_harness.cc) - Rope->rotary stitch operator (rope_stitch.cc / rope_stitch.cu) - Scheduler changes to consult adapter decisions (routing.py / scheduler.cc) - Tests and perf harness (tests/attn/test_probe.py, perf/attn_adapter_bench.py) - Docs (docs/perf/attn_adapter.md)

Files changed (high-level): redwood/serve/attn/adapter.py, redwood/serve/attn/adapter.h, redwood/serve/attn/probe_kern.cu, redwood/serve/attn/probe_harness.cc, redwood/serve/attn/rope_stitch.cc, redwood/serve/attn/rope_stitch.cu, redwood/serve/scheduler/routing.py, redwood/serve/scheduler/scheduler.cc, tests/attn/test_probe.py, perf/attn_adapter_bench.py, docs/perf/attn_adapter.md, setup/ci/attn-probe-matrix.yml

Review thread (highlights): Lina Gómez (reviewer): "Nice separation of concerns. Two asks: 1) add a deterministic seed and additional assertions in test_probe to avoid flakiness we saw in canary; 2) make the adapter fallback path explicitly opt-out via feature flag so we can A/B on Dedicated." Daniel Hsu (author): "Added deterministic RNG seed and strengthened assertions (tests updated). Feature toggle added: ATTN_ADAPTER_ROLLOUT env + runtime config; default off for Dedicated. See adapter.py lines ~120-145." Evan Park (reviewer): "Kernel probe harness looks solid; I'm concerned about the timeout semantics on extremely loaded hosts (we saw a 30ms probe stall last week). Can we bound probe to a pooled worker and fail-safe?" Daniel Hsu: "Probe now runs on a bounded worker thread with a 12ms soft timeout and a 50ms hard timeout; on timeout we log once per boot and mark fused ops as unavailable. This is documented in probe_harness.cc and in docs/perf/attn_adapter.md." Maya Singh (reviewer): "Perf numbers look promising; please add a perf dashboard link and note the GPU types where gains were measured." Daniel Hsu: "Added benchmark CSV and Grafana panel link to the docs; numbers: 6-12% p50 improvement, 8-18% p99 improvement on mixed-length chat workloads on A100/H100 with rope sizes <=64."

CI summary: - build: pass - unit-tests: pass (1 flaky kernel test required rerun) - lint: pass - integration-tests: pass - perf-microbench: pass (bench harness runs; recorded improvements) Note: initial CI run failed on a CUDA 11.7 build due to an ABI test; fixed by pinning a sub-dependency and reran — subsequent runs passed.

Performance notes: Benchmarks run with canonical chat workload (turn-taking messages with 8/32/512 histories). The adapter prefers fused rope_stitch for rotary dim <=64 and sequence lengths 256-2048 where the fused path reduces kernel launch overhead. Measured by perf harness: p50 improved 6-12%, p99 improved 8-18% depending on model and batch mix. Cost analysis: small increase in binary size (~120KB) and negligible runtime memory for probe tables; win is reduced token CPU/GPU cycles for short sequences.

Compatibility and rollout: Backwards-compatible. The fused rope_stitch has explicit fallback to per-layer rotary application when not available. A feature flag (ATTN_ADAPTER_ROLLOUT) controls automatic use; rollout plan recommends starting at 0% on Dedicated and 25% on Hosted with monitoring for regressed eval prompts.

Known limitations & follow-ups: - Current stitch operator targets rope sizes up to 128; follow-up work tracked in ENG-4993 to extend to larger rope shards and AVX2 fallbacks for CPU. - Add tighter perf regression alerts in the console (TODO tracked in ENG-5040). - Investigate micro-batching interactions with the adapter for very high throughput steady traffic (ENG-5072).

Merge: after reviewer approvals and CI green, merged via squash on 2026-02-25.

If you're validating locally: see docs/perf/attn_adapter.md for how to run the probe harness and perf scripts.
